title: Choose Fender's visual world
question: Which direction makes Fender feel simple, informative, and unmistakably built for trustworthy coding work?

options.label: Engineer's Job Docket
options.lineage: Field-service job cards, inspection dockets, and release sign-off sheets
options.thesis: One task sheet gathers every action, exception, and proof until it earns a signed outcome.
options.viewport: A single oversized task docket owns the center; attached slips reveal activity, changes, tests, and completion evidence only as they exist.
options.risk: It becomes bureaucratic or skeuomorphic if the job-card metaphor outranks speed and familiar controls.

options.label: One-Bit Workbench
options.lineage: Early monochrome desktops, dithered system tools, and compact developer utilities
options.thesis: Fender becomes a crisp black-and-white desktop where one task window contains every state.
options.viewport: One main task window with compact tiled inspectors and no overlapping-window clutter.
options.risk: Nostalgia and high contrast can overpower accessibility, clarity, and modern calm.
options.case: Developer identification is immediate, but nostalgic window grammar weakens calm product clarity.

options.label: Signal Bench
options.lineage: Oscilloscopes, signal benches, and scientific diagnostic instruments
options.thesis: The run becomes one measured signal, with tools, child work, tests, and failures aligned on a diagnostic trace.
options.viewport: One wide diagnostic screen joins the task and composer to a restrained execution trace.
options.risk: Continuous signal imagery can turn runtime truth into decorative monitoring.
options.case: The diagnostic identity is strong, but discrete tasks and evidence do not naturally behave like one waveform.

options.label: Iridescent Edge
options.lineage: Cloud light, auroras, and restrained spectral edge conditions
options.thesis: A quiet white work surface reveals narrow spectral bands only where state or attention changes.
options.viewport: A spacious task canvas uses a spectral status edge to disclose activity and evidence layers.
options.risk: It can collapse into generic pastel minimalism with weak developer identification.
options.case: Calm and clarity are excellent, but the visual world says little about serious coding work.

canonCard.label: Modern Agent IDE
canonCard.lineage: Contemporary code editors and AI-agent sidebars
canonCard.thesis: A polished dark coding-agent workbench with a sidebar, central chat, activity panel, and status bar.
canonCard.viewport: A familiar project sidebar, central conversation, right-side activity inspector, and bottom composer.
canonCard.risk: It is immediately familiar, but indistinguishable from existing AI IDEs.
